caption:
I review a lot of React code where every value is wrapped in useMemo "for performance".

For cheap work like filtering 20 items or joining two strings, the comparison costs about as much as just doing the work again.

How to decide: measure first. React's docs suggest wrapping a calculation in console.time and memoizing only if it takes a noticeable amount of time (around 1 ms or more).

Source: react.dev, useMemo.

Where have you seen useMemo overused?

altText:
useMemo is not free.

On every render React still compares the dependency array and keeps the old value in memory.

Wrap the one slow calculation. Not every variable.
